<div id="m12-explain" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<dl class="lx-ideas">
<dt>The hub</dt><dd>Each district-hour, electricity bought through the substation, rooftop sun and batteries meet the base load, heating and car charging.</dd>
<dt>Building shares</dt><dd>Heat is split into shares by envelope and heating system, so heating power is linear in the decisions.</dd>
<dt>The substation's ceiling</dt><dd>Each hour's purchase stays under the limit plus any upgrade; its dual is the value of one more MW of room in that hour.</dd>
<dt>The cap's dual</dt><dd>When the LP chooses under a CO₂ cap, the cap's dual is the cost of the last tonne cut, under this model's assumptions.</dd>
<dt>Kept apart</dt><dd>Bills and energy burden by household group come from an accounting layer after the LP, with a stated rule for who adopts first.</dd>
<dt>The full-year check</dt><dd>The four plans, run again on every hour of 2025 with what the eight days decided kept: total cost and CO₂ hold; the upgrades the eight days buy fall a little short on 19 or 20 February.</dd>
<dt>What it tests</dt><dd>The year is scaled, like the days, to the same annual heat and base energy, so cost and CO₂ hold partly by construction: it checks the hours' timing.</dd>
</dl>

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>The hub in symbols</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

Every hour lasts $\Delta t = 1$ h, so a MW held for an hour is a MWh. Days $k$ (8), hours $h$ (24), districts $d$ (3).

::: {.lx-scroll-x .m12-symbols}
| Symbol | What it is | Unit | Decided or given |
|---|---|---|---|
| $imp_{dkh}$ | bought through district $d$'s substation | MW | decided, $\ge 0$ |
| $pv_{dkh}$, $ev_{dkh}$ | rooftop solar used; car charging (managed) | MW | decided |
| $c_{dkh}$, $o_{dkh}$, $q_{dkh}$ | battery in, out, stored | MW, MW, MWh | decided |
| $y_{d,e,s}$ | share of district $d$'s heat in envelope $e$ (0 as built, 1 retrofitted) with system $s$ | share | given in a run; decided in step 6 |
| $up_d$ | upgrade of $d$'s substation | MW | decided |
| $w_k$ | days day $k$ stands for (they add to 365) | days | given |
| $p_d$, $p_{ind}$, $a$ | $d$'s 2025 electricity price; the industrial price the network's plant pays; the upgrade's yearly cost | \$/MWh; \$/MWh; \$ per MW a year | given |
| $B_{dkh}$, $Q_{dkh}$ | base load; heat needed: the hour's temperature deficit below 18.3 °C × the heat-loss rate (MW of heat per °C) | MW; MW of heat | given (prairie-city.json) |
| $\sigma$, $COP_{kh}$ | heat a retrofit saves; the heat pump's coefficient of performance (heat out per unit of electricity in) | share; MWh/MWh | given |
| $L_d$, $S_{dkh}$, $E_{dk}$ | substation limit; rooftop output; the day's charging energy | MW; MW; MWh | given |
| $pl_{kh}$ | the heat network's plant power (core only): its heat pump's heat $\div$ 3 | MW | decided |
| $hp_{kh}$, $boil_{kh}$, $si_{kh}$, $so_{kh}$ | the network's heat pump, gas boiler (assumed to exist: fuel only), store in and out | MW of heat | decided |
:::

$$\min\; \sum_k w_k \sum_h \Big[\sum_d p_d\, imp_{dkh} + (p_{ind} - p_{core})\, pl_{kh}\Big] \;+\; a \sum_d up_d \;+\; \text{fuel}(y, boil) \;[+\; \text{equipment}(y, \text{sizes})]$$

The plant's power comes through the core's substation but is bought at the industrial price: the second term swaps one price for the other. Fuel is the furnaces' gas and propane (set by $y$) and the network boiler's gas: $\sum_k w_k \sum_h boil_{kh} \div 0.9$ at the commercial gas price.

Each district-hour (the balance). Its dual carries the day's weight $w_k$: divided by $w_k$, it is the marginal cost of one more MWh in one such hour, as the engine reports it. The substation duals stay summed over the year, in \$ per MW a year.

$$imp + pv + o - c - ev - \sum_{e,s} Q_{dkh}\,(1 - \sigma e)\; y_{d,e,s}\;\kappa_s - [d = \text{core}]\, pl_{kh} = B_{dkh}, \qquad \kappa_{res} = 1,\; \kappa_{hp} = \frac{1}{COP_{kh}},\; \kappa_{fuel} = \kappa_{dh} = 0$$

The heat network in the core (its own heat balance, with 10% lost in the pipes and a store that loses 0.5% an hour):

$$hp_{kh} + boil_{kh} + so_{kh} - si_{kh} = \frac{1}{0.9}\sum_{e} Q_{\text{core},kh}\,(1 - \sigma e)\; y_{\text{core},e,dh}, \qquad pl_{kh} = \frac{hp_{kh}}{3}$$

The substation (its dual: what one more MW of room is worth that hour), the sun, the battery and the day's charging:

$$imp_{dkh} - up_d \le L_d, \qquad pv_{dkh} \le S_{dkh}, \qquad q_{dkh} = q_{dk,h-1} + 0.85\, c_{dkh} - o_{dkh},\; q_{dk,-1} = q_{dk,23}, \qquad \sum_h ev_{dkh} = E_{dk}$$

When the LP chooses (step 6): $\sum_{e,s} y_{d,e,s} = 1$, furnaces and resistance no more than in 2025, retrofits and district heat up to their maxima, and $\text{CO}_2(imp, y) \le cap$. Shares sit inside the LP in percent (0 to 100), which keeps HiGHS's numbers close in size.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>When two answers cost the same: the tie rule</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
<p>With one price all day, many schedules tie. Small stated costs pick one; they are left out of every reported cost total, though the duals include them:</p>
<div class="lx-scroll-x"><table class="lx-facts m12-ties"><thead><tr><th scope="col">Tie cost</th><th scope="col">Size</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>Each district's busiest hour</td><td class="n">$20 a year per MW</td></tr>
<tr><td>The three districts' busiest hour together</td><td class="n">$10 per MW</td></tr>
<tr><td>Out of a battery</td><td class="n">$1 per MWh</td></tr>
<tr><td>Out of the heat store</td><td class="n">$0.50 per MWh</td></tr>
<tr><td>Managed charging</td><td class="n">$0.10 per MWh × the hour's share of SPP's peak demand</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>
<ul class="m12-rules">
<li>The LP minimizes the cost plus these small costs: on a few plans it pays under $30 a year, in the engine's test, to keep a busiest hour that is under its limit lower.</li>
<li>The engine's test finds the lowest and highest value of each busiest hour, each upgrade and the energy bought over every plan within $1 of the best cost: they agree within its tolerances (0.5 MW, 0.05 MW and 5 MWh).</li>
<li>The tie costs also enter the balance duals, by a few dollars at most on the busiest hours: read them as "about".</li>
<li>The substation duals summed over the year are checked as slopes of the LP's objective, cost plus the tie costs: it moves by the same amount when the limit moves 0.1 MW up or down.</li>
<li>The reported cost leaves the tie costs out: where a limit binds without an upgrade, it saves about $9 per MW a year more than the dual.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Researcher</span>Where this model stops</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
<ul class="m12-rules">
<li>One ceiling per substation stands for a whole distribution network; real planning checks each feeder's power flow and voltage (<a href="a17-physical-feasibility.html">A17</a>).</li>
<li>Each day ends with the stored energy it started with, a level the LP picks day by day, on the eight days and in the full-year check: no heat or charge carried between days.</li>
<li>The full-year check uses the same synthetic weather rule: it tests the choice of days, not another weather year.</li>
<li>The base load follows the whole regional grid's 2025 shape, which keeps some of its winter electric heating: winter peaks and upgrades are illustrative.</li>
<li>Many plans cost nearly the same; methods that map near-optimal plans show the choice is wider than one optimum.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</details>
</div>

<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="m12-myths">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="kwh" data-answer="myth"><p class="lx-qtext">Electrifying heat only adds yearly kWh; the grid sees a small rise.</p><ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. Cold weather, when heat pumps' COP is low, lifts heating in every home at once; with the base load and car charging it sets the busiest hour (06:00 or 20:00 here), which the yearly total hides.</p></details></div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="dual" data-answer="fact"><p class="lx-qtext">Where the LP buys an upgrade, the substation's duals summed over the year equal the upgrade's yearly cost per MW.</p><ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Fact. One more MW of limit saves one MW of upgrade; the test checks it as a cost slope both ways.</p></details></div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="burden" data-answer="myth"><p class="lx-qtext">The LP tells you how a plan changes each household group's energy burden.</p><ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. The LP gives the city's cost, CO₂ and peaks; who pays comes from an accounting layer with its own stated assumptions.</p></details></div>
</div>
```
